Golden Gate Park is one of San Francisco's liveliest greenspaces, and these four neighborhoods are ideal for those who want to live right next door.

Directly south of Golden Gate Park is San Francisco’s Sunset District, considered by many to be a quieter fringe neighborhood removed from the noise of the city. Known for its fog—even more so than the rest of San Francisco—the Sunset is divided by 19th Avenue, so if you live here, you either live in Inner Sunset (east of 19th) or Outer Sunset (west of 19th).

San Francisco's most seductively situated museum, the Legion is set on ocean bluffs at Land's End with sweeping views of the Golden Gate. The neoclassical museum is a three-quarter-scale adaptation of the 18th-century Palais de la Légion d'Honneur in Paris, built in 1924 as a memorial to the Californians who died in World War I.
